title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RICK IS LATE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rick, a pool cleaner in Fort Myers, Florida.
Everybody loves Rick. There's just one problem. Rick is always late.
He was even late to his own wedding.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE GREEN POOL
segments.quote: Time is what we want most, but what, alas, we use worst.
segments.author: William Penn
lines: His biggest customer, Mrs. Delaney, runs the Palm Breeze Motel.
One morning she waited two hours, while her guests stared at a green pool.
By her desk hung a saying from William Penn, who founded Pennsylvania. She tapped it.
Time is what we want most, but what, alas, we use worst.
One more late morning, Rick, and I call somebody else.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE EXCUSES
segments.quote: I attribute my success to this: I never gave or took an excuse.
segments.author: Florence Nightingale
lines: That week, Rick was late again. Traffic. A flat tire. A dog that ate his hose.
His wife Carmen, a nurse, slid her Florence Nightingale mug across the table:
I attribute my success to this: I never gave or took an excuse.
So Rick stopped making excuses, and started fixing reasons. A spare tire. A fence for the hose.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NIGHT BEFORE
segments.quote: The beginning is the most important part of the work.
segments.author: Plato
lines: His mornings were chaos. Where's the chlorine? Where are my sunglasses? On his head.
His fishing buddy Walt quoted Plato, the old Greek thinker:
The beginning is the most important part of the work.
So Rick packed the truck the night before. Out the door at seven sharp.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PHONE
segments.quote: Concentrate all your thoughts upon the work at hand. The sun's rays do not burn until brought to a focus.
segments.author: Alexander Graham Bell
lines: But his phone buzzed all day, and every pool got half his attention.
Then the radio quoted Alexander Graham Bell, who invented the telephone:
Concentrate all your thoughts upon the work at hand. The sun's rays do not burn until brought to a focus.
Even the phone guy says put down the phone. Into the glove box it went.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE SNOOZE
segments.quote: Habit is a cable. We weave a thread of it every day, and at last we cannot break it.
segments.author: Horace Mann
lines: Three good weeks. Then one morning, his hand found the snooze button.
He remembered a sign at the bait shop, from Horace Mann, a famous American educator:
Habit is a cable. We weave a thread of it every day, and at last we cannot break it.
So Rick moved the alarm clock across the room. Snoozing now required a hike.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FREE HOUR
segments.quote: A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life.
segments.author: Charles Darwin
lines: Six months later, Rick pulled into the Palm Breeze early. Mrs. Delaney nearly dropped her coffee.
She sent him three new motels. And Rick was home by five, fishing with his son.
On the boat, Walt read from a letter by the young Charles Darwin:
A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life.
Rick looked at his boy. He'd finally discovered it.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Value time. No excuses. Start right. Focus. Build the habit. Live the hours.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Value your time. Drop the excuses. Start right. Focus. Build the habit. And spend the saved hours on people you love.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. Rick says hi. He got here early.
